solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Time for new-age celebrations that can make customers smile

indicators.note: what the letters can make is a new word built from them rearranged

explanation.surface: A shop's promotional gimmick for midsummer pagan revels that might cheer the shoppers.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of CUSTOMERS SMILE rearrange to give the answer; 'that' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Druids and new-age followers gather at Stonehenge on the longest day of the year, the June solstice.

clue.text: Speaker's position on raised pay

parts.note: a political speaker campaigning is 'on the stump', a tree stump once used as a platform
raised means up

explanation.surface: A speaker of the House taking a stand on a pay rise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Speaker's' suggests a sound-alike, but here it is just a public orator, whose platform is the stump.
explanation.definitionFit: To stump up is an informal phrase meaning to hand over money, often reluctantly.

clue.text: Red number held up in place of trade, and another in catalogue

indicators.note: the number sits in the market, inside its letters

parts.note: a mart is a market, a place of trade

indicators.note: in a down clue, held up means the word six is read from bottom to top

parts.note: six is a number

indicators.note: the second number goes in the catalogue, inside its letters

parts.note: a list is a catalogue
another number, nine, also held up, so read upwards in the down light

explanation.surface: A communist number, a radical figure, among traders and listed in an index.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held up' does double duty for both numbers: nine read upwards also goes in the catalogue, sitting after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Red is a common shorthand for a communist, and a follower of Marx and Lenin's doctrine is a communist.

clue.text: What's liable to cause shock when it's shown up?

definitions.text: What's liable to cause shock when it's shown up?

indicators.note: in a down light, shown up means the word is written upwards, so read backwards

parts.note: a live wire or terminal is liable to give an electric shock

explanation.surface: A riddle about what gives you a jolt once it is exposed.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a whole, wickedness shocks people when it is exposed; read as wordplay, LIVE turned upwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Wickedness, once revealed, shocks people, so the whole clue describes moral badness.

clue.text: Fluctuate as witness — and did so in the past

parts.note: to witness is to see
did so, that is witnessed, in the past tense is saw

explanation.surface: A wavering witness who changes their account of what they saw.
explanation.definitionFit: To seesaw is to move up and down or back and forth, swinging between states.

clue.text: Group of youngsters with limited education created mess

parts.note: a litter is a group of young animals born together
ed is the shortened, limited form of education

explanation.surface: Poorly schooled kids leaving a place in a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Youngsters' suggests children, but a litter is a brood of puppies or kittens.
explanation.definitionFit: Littered means scattered rubbish about, so made a place untidy.

clue.text: One expelled from school and criticized moved elsewhere

indicators.note: the one is thrown out of the word for school, as a pupil is expelled

parts.note: to school someone is to train them
one is the Roman numeral I
slated means harshly criticized

explanation.surface: A pupil expelled and condemned who then left the area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'School' looks like a noun but is the verb, train; taking out I leaves TRAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Translated in its older sense means moved from one place to another, as a bishop or relic is transferred.

clue.text: Work on furniture put on display

definitions.text: Work on furniture put on display

parts.words: Work on furniture put on display
parts.note: a book (a work) left on a low table in the sitting room so guests can see it

explanation.walkthrough: 'Work on furniture' sounds like carpentry, but the work is a published book.
explanation.definitionFit: A large illustrated volume meant for casual browsing is kept on a low lounge table to impress visitors.

clue.text: Through a lucky chance acquiring new servant

indicators.note: the lucky word acquires, takes in, the letter for new

parts.note: fluky means happening through a lucky chance

explanation.surface: Someone who hired a new servant by sheer luck.
explanation.definitionFit: A flunky is a liveried manservant or, by extension, an obsequious underling.

clue.text: Our weather feature heading East for European country

parts.note: for a British newspaper, our country is the UK
rain is a familiar feature of British weather
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: British rain moving east towards a country on the continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading' is a link word: the East comes last, not at the head.
explanation.definitionFit: Ukraine is a large nation in eastern Europe bordering Russia and Poland.

clue.text: Visibly distressed after end of test, getting reprimand

indicators.note: the end of test is its final letter

parts.note: an earful is a telling-off, a reprimand

explanation.surface: A pupil upset after an exam, then scolded on top of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone tearful is crying or close to it, so their upset shows plainly.

clue.text: Song with piano accompaniment for duo

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, here accompanying the song
an air is a song or tune

explanation.surface: A song with piano backing, performed by two musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair is two of something, the same as a duo or couple.

clue.text: E.g. Chinese food at back of vessel

parts.note: fare is food
astern means at or towards the rear of a ship

explanation.surface: A Chinese takeaway being eaten at the rear of a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chinese food' looks like one phrase, but 'Chinese' is the definition and 'food' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: China lies in the Orient, so something Chinese is an example of what is from East Asia.

clue.text: Something inserted in a pot I ordered — it's a shrub

indicators.note: the something is inserted into the rearranged letters
the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: an inset is something set in, which the clue's 'inserted' confirms

explanation.surface: A plant put into a pot that I had bought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' suggests buying, but it is the signal to rearrange A POT I.
explanation.definitionFit: The poinsettia is a Mexican plant with red bracts, popular at Christmas, which grows as a bush in the wild.

clue.text: Poignancy seen among group at hospital

indicators.note: the answer is seen among the letters of the following words

explanation.surface: A touching scene witnessed among a party of hospital visitors.
explanation.definitionFit: Pathos is the quality in art or life that stirs pity and sadness.

clue.text: Nitpicking editor shut in small room

indicators.note: the editor is shut inside the small room

parts.note: a pantry is a small room for storing food

explanation.surface: A fussy editor locked in a tiny room to check proofs.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedantry is excessive fussing over small details and rules, the habit of a quibbler.

clue.text: During endless fight, snide comment is demeaning

parts.note: in means during, as in 'in the night'

indicators.note: the word for fight loses its final letter

parts.note: a fray is a fight or brawl
a dig is a snide remark

explanation.surface: Making a cutting remark in the middle of a scrap is beneath you.
explanation.walkthrough: Infra dig, from Latin infra dignitatem, means beneath one's dignity.
explanation.definitionFit: Something beneath one's dignity is degrading or humiliating to do.

clue.text: Collecting left-overs is good tendency

parts.note: a leaning is a tendency or inclination

explanation.surface: A remark that saving scraps is a fine habit.
explanation.definitionFit: Gleaning is gathering grain left behind after harvest, so picking up remnants.

clue.text: Parts of house beginning to buckle in strong winds

indicators.note: the first letter goes in the word for strong winds

parts.note: gales are strong winds

indicators.note: the beginning of buckle is its first letter

explanation.surface: Bits of a house starting to give way in a storm.
explanation.definitionFit: Gables are the triangular wall sections at the ends of a pitched roof.

clue.text: A bishop dividing family — one can sink no lower than that

definitions.text: one can sink no lower than that

indicators.note: A and B divide the family word, sitting inside it

parts.note: seed in the biblical sense means offspring, descendants
B is the chess notation for bishop

explanation.surface: A churchman causing a rift in a household, the lowest of the low.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads like moral disgrace, but it is literal: a sinking object stops at the bottom of the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The ocean floor is the lowest point a sinking ship or stone can reach.

clue.text: Middle piece of cotton garment worn long ago

indicators.note: the middle piece of the word cotton is its central pair of letters, which are the same letter twice

parts.note: the word cotton, whose middle is two Ts

explanation.surface: The central section of a cotton garment from a bygone age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Middle piece of cotton' is what the answer's wordplay produces: the centre of COTTON is two Ts, a double T.
explanation.definitionFit: A doublet was a close-fitting padded jacket worn by men in Renaissance times.

clue.text: Auntie engaged in hugging old feline

indicators.note: the broadcaster's letters hug the old, holding it inside

parts.note: Auntie is a British nickname for the BBC
at means engaged in, as in 'at work'

explanation.surface: An aunt busy cuddling an elderly cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Auntie' is the affectionate British nickname for the BBC, the national broadcaster.
explanation.definitionFit: The bobcat is a North American wild cat with a short tail.

clue.text: One or two people starting a union

definitions.text: One or two people starting a union

parts.words: One or two people starting a union
parts.note: a marriage is a union begun by two people, and this is one of that couple

explanation.walkthrough: 'Union' suggests a trade union; the union is a wedding, and the answer is one of the pair.
explanation.definitionFit: The man getting married is one of the two people whose wedding begins their marriage.

clue.text: Something little boy uses to inspire passion, it's said, in sweetheart

indicators.note: it's said means the word is spoken and we write what it sounds like

parts.words: Something little boy uses to inspire passion
parts.note: Cupid, the little boy god of love, shoots arrows from his bow

explanation.surface: Cupid using his tools to stir love in someone's darling.
explanation.walkthrough: The little boy is Cupid, whose bow sounds like the French-derived word for a boyfriend.
explanation.definitionFit: A beau is a boyfriend or male admirer, a lover.

clue.text: Part in opera Callas initially rejected

indicators.note: the initial, first letter is rejected, dropped

parts.note: Maria Callas was the celebrated Greek-American soprano

explanation.surface: The diva Callas turned down for a role in an opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part' suggests a role, but it is a solo piece; Callas gives her first name.
explanation.definitionFit: An aria is a solo song forming one section of an opera.

clue.text: Was left holding pole

indicators.note: the word for left holds the pole inside

parts.note: exited means left, went out
S, south, is one of the poles

explanation.surface: Someone who departed carrying a pole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' looks like the direction, but it is the verb, went out.
explanation.definitionFit: Was, in the sense of 'there was', means was in being, lived.

clue.text: Repeat both sides of festive music, amusing Oxford don

indicators.note: both sides are right and left, R and L, and each is repeated

parts.note: a carol is a Christmas song

explanation.surface: A pun about playing a Christmas record over again on each side.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'sides' sound like a record's, but they are Right and Left: double each in CAROL.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewis Carroll, pen name of the mathematician Charles Dodgson, lectured at Christ Church and wrote the comic Alice books.

clue.text: Honest alien holding flag put under severe restraint

indicators.note: honest plus alien hold the flag inside, between them

parts.note: straight means honest
ET is the film extraterrestrial
a jack is a flag flown at a ship's bow

explanation.surface: A truthful extraterrestrial with a banner who is put in restraints.
explanation.definitionFit: To straightjacket someone is to bind them in a canvas garment that pins the arms, so to confine harshly.
